category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.rationale: 'The most common Grade-1 trap on C3.1 is the unordered-list error...' — trap is concrete and recovery is actionable, but no research citation and recovery_moves do not branch by diagnostic.
category_feedback.required_fix: Cite a named source (e.g., Bers 2018 ScratchJr studies, Kazakoff & Bers on early sequencing, or NRC 2011 'Computational Thinking' framework) and branch recovery_moves: if child writes narrative-not-actions, drop to 'finger-act each step'; if child orders correctly but skips a step, use 'check Coda's hands' diagnostic.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: consolidation.exit_routine: 'Each child writes ONE 3-step code on a sticky note... Notes go on the chart.' Coda anchors every segment but has no quotable refrain or memorable chant carried between lessons.
category_feedback.required_fix: Give Coda a signature opening/closing chant children echo (e.g., 'Coda says: STEP, by STEP, by STEP — that's CODE!') and embed it in minds_on hook AND consolidation exit_routine so the refrain travels into Lessons 2-5.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: action.steps[3]: 'Right, then up vs up, then right — same ending square. So order doesn't ALWAYS matter for movement.' — strong conceptual move, but expanded_walkthrough does not name the misconception in research-grounded terms.
category_feedback.required_fix: In expanded_walkthrough.rationale, name the underlying construct using research-grounded terms — e.g., Papert's 'computational sequencing' or Bers' 'Powerful Ideas of CS' framework on order/sequencing — and frame the trap as a sequencing-vs-listing distinction explicitly.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: worksheet pages[0].parts: Part 1 (5-step task), Part 2 (execute 4 grids), Part 3 (invent task). Worksheet parallels lesson stations 1:1 but does not deliberately VARY format as a transfer task and gives no justification for a generalization probe.
category_feedback.required_fix: Modify Part 2 or Part 3 to include a clearly-justified transfer twist (e.g., Part 2 grid 4 introduces a NEW direction the lesson didn't drill, or Part 3 prompts 'write code for someone else to follow' to verify generalization) and add a teacher_notes line naming the transfer rationale.

summary: Pair 1 has strong alignment to C3.1 and excellent instructional balance (everyday materials, BE-Coda no-paper variant). However, pedagogical_depth needs research grounding and branched recovery; clarity_voice needs a Coda signature refrain that travels across lessons; mathematical_authenticity needs the misconception named in research terms; and the worksheet parallels rather than transfers the lesson's practice. Multiple categories at 3 — revise both lesson and worksheet.
